paragraphs.title: The One Language and the Building of Babel

easy.question: What was the condition of the whole earth at the beginning of this passage?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the whole earth had one language and one speech.

easy.question: Where did the people find a plain and settle?
easy.explanation: They found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

easy.question: What did the people want to build?
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Let us build us a city and a tower.”

medium.question: What did the people do after finding a plain in the land of Shinar?
answers: They returned to their former home
medium.explanation: After finding the plain, they settled there.

medium.question: In the phrase “Go to, let us make brick,” what does “Go to” mean?
answers: Come, or let us do it
medium.explanation: “Go to” is an invitation to act together and begin the work.

medium.question: Why did the people want to build a city and a tower?
answers: So that they would not be scattered over the earth
medium.explanation: They said they wanted to avoid being scattered over the face of the whole earth.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the building materials described in verse 3?
answers: They used brick instead of stone and slime as mortar
They did not know how to make building materials
challenge.explanation: The verse says that they used brick for stone and slime for mortar.

challenge.question: How did their one language help the people?
answers: It allowed them to plan and work together
challenge.explanation: Because everyone spoke the same language, they could agree and cooperate in building the city and tower.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “whose top may reach unto heaven” convey?
answers: The tower was made of clouds
They wanted to build a very high tower
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the great height they intended for the tower.

answers: They used brick instead of stone and slime as mortar
They did not know how to make building materials
questions.explanation: The verse says that they used brick for stone and slime for mortar.

questions.question: How did their one language help the people?
answers: It allowed them to plan and work together
questions.explanation: Because everyone spoke the same language, they could agree and cooperate in building the city and tower.

questions.question: What does the phrase “whose top may reach unto heaven” convey?
answers: The tower was made of clouds

questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the great height they intended for the tower.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Sees the City and the Tower

easy.question: Why did the Lord come down, according to the verse?
answers: To see the city and the tower
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord came down to see the city and tower built by the people.

easy.question: Who built the city and the tower?
easy.explanation: The verse specifically says they were built by the children of men.

easy.question: What did all the people have in common?
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “The people is one, and they have all one language.”

medium.question: Why was it said that nothing would be restrained from them that they imagined to do?
answers: Because they had a tall tower
Because they were one people with one language
Because the Lord helped them build
medium.explanation: Their unity and common language enabled them to cooperate and carry out their plans.

medium.question: In the phrase “this they begin to do,” what does “begin” indicate?
answers: This was only the beginning of their actions
medium.explanation: The statement points to the fact that their building project was only the beginning of what they might attempt.

medium.question: What happened after the Lord came down to see the city and the tower?
answers: He said that the people were one and had one language
medium.explanation: After seeing the city and tower, the Lord observed that the people were united and shared one language.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do”?
answers: They had already completed all their plans
The Lord approved everything they did
Their unity gave them great ability to carry out plans
challenge.explanation: The statement emphasizes how difficult it would be to stop people who are united and understand one another.

challenge.question: Why does the verse mention both the city and the tower?
answers: To emphasize the scale of their building project
To say that there were two peoples
To show that the city was far from the tower
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both structures presents the large construction project the people had undertaken.

challenge.question: What does “they have all one language” emphasize?
answers: Only the leaders understood one another
Everyone in the people shared the same language
Each person had a private language
challenge.explanation: The statement makes clear that the common language belonged to all the people.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do”?
answers: They had already completed all their plans

Their unity gave them great ability to carry out plans
questions.explanation: The statement emphasizes how difficult it would be to stop people who are united and understand one another.

questions.question: Why does the verse mention both the city and the tower?
answers: To emphasize the scale of their building project

To show that the city was far from the tower
questions.explanation: Mentioning both structures presents the large construction project the people had undertaken.

answers: Only the leaders understood one another

paragraphs.title: The Confusion of Languages and the Scattering of Humanity

easy.question: What did the Lord do to the language of the city’s people?
answers: He taught them a new language
He restored one language to them
easy.explanation: The Lord confused their language, so they could no longer understand one another’s speech.

easy.question: What did the people stop doing?
easy.explanation: After the Lord confused their language, they stopped building the city.

easy.question: Why was the city called Babel?
answers: It was the largest city in the land
It was built on a hill
The Lord confused the language of all the earth there
easy.explanation: The verse explains that the name is connected with the confusion of language there.

medium.question: What was the order of events in these verses?
answers: The language was confused, building stopped, and the people were scattered
The people were scattered, the city was built, and the language was confused
Building stopped, the language was confused, and the city was built
medium.explanation: First the language was confused, then they stopped building, and finally the Lord scattered them over the earth.

medium.question: What did the Lord’s command “let us go down, and there confound their language” mean?
answers: Let us write down their language
medium.explanation: The command means that the Lord would confuse their language so they would not understand one another.

medium.question: Why did the confusion of language cause the people to stop building the city?
answers: They were afraid of the city
They could not understand one another
medium.explanation: Without understanding one another’s speech, they could not cooperate in building the city.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated phrase “from thence”?
answers: The scattering began at the place where they built the city
The people repeatedly returned to the same place
The city was built in several different places
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the place where the language was confused became the starting point for their scattering.

challenge.question: What does “upon the face of all the earth” emphasize?
answers: The scattering was widespread and not limited to the city
The city was larger than the whole earth
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the Lord scattered the people to many places throughout the earth.

challenge.question: What does the verse explain about the name Babel?
answers: The name recalls the confusion of language there
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the city’s name with the Lord’s confusing the language of all the earth.

questions.question: What can be understood from the repeated phrase “from thence”?
answers: The scattering began at the place where they built the city
The people repeatedly returned to the same place
The city was built in several different places
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the place where the language was confused became the starting point for their scattering.

questions.question: What does “upon the face of all the earth” emphasize?
answers: The scattering was widespread and not limited to the city
The city was larger than the whole earth
questions.explanation: The phrase shows that the Lord scattered the people to many places throughout the earth.

questions.question: What does the verse explain about the name Babel?
answers: The name recalls the confusion of language there
questions.explanation: The verse connects the city’s name with the Lord’s confusing the language of all the earth.

paragraphs.title: The Line of Shem to Eber

easy.question: Who was the father of Arphaxad?
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says that Shem begat Arphaxad.

easy.question: How old was Arphaxad when he begat Salah?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Arphaxad lived thirty-five years and begat Salah.

easy.question: Whom did Eber begat?
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says that Eber begat Peleg.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the generations in these verses?
medium.explanation: Each man became the father of the next: Shem begat Arphaxad, who begat Salah, and so on.

medium.question: What does “These are the generations of Shem” mean here?
medium.explanation: The phrase introduces a list of Shem’s descendants.

medium.question: Who was older when he begat the son mentioned: Salah or Eber?
medium.explanation: Salah begat Eber at thirty, while Eber begat Peleg at thirty-four.

challenge.question: About how old was Shem at the time of the Flood?
challenge.explanation: Shem begat Arphaxad two years after the Flood at age one hundred, so he was about ninety-eight at the Flood.

challenge.question: Who lived the longest after begetting the son mentioned?
challenge.explanation: Eber lived 430 years after begetting Peleg, compared with 403 years for Arphaxad and Salah.

challenge.question: How long did Eber live in total, according to the verses?
challenge.explanation: Eber was thirty-four when he begat Peleg and lived another 430 years, for a total of 464.

questions.question: About how old was Shem at the time of the Flood?
questions.explanation: Shem begat Arphaxad two years after the Flood at age one hundred, so he was about ninety-eight at the Flood.

questions.question: How long did Eber live in total, according to the verses?
questions.explanation: Eber was thirty-four when he begat Peleg and lived another 430 years, for a total of 464.

easy.question: Whom did Peleg begat?
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says that Peleg begat Reu.

easy.question: How old was Peleg when he begat Reu?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Peleg lived thirty years and begat Reu.

easy.question: Whom did Nahor begat?
easy.explanation: Verse 24 says that Nahor begat Terah.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the generations from Peleg to Terah?
medium.explanation: Peleg begat Reu, Reu begat Serug, Serug begat Nahor, and Nahor begat Terah.

medium.question: What does “after he begat Serug” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the time after Reu begat Serug and became his father.

medium.question: How many years older was Reu than Nahor when each begat the son mentioned?
medium.explanation: Reu begat Serug at thirty-two, while Nahor begat Terah at twenty-nine, a difference of three years.

challenge.question: How long did Reu live in total, according to the verses?
challenge.explanation: Reu lived thirty-two years before begetting Serug and another 207 years afterward, totaling 239.

challenge.question: Which of these people lived the fewest years?
challenge.explanation: Nahor lived twenty-nine years before begetting Terah and another 119 years, totaling 148 years.

challenge.question: Which two people lived the same number of years in total?
challenge.explanation: Peleg lived 30 plus 209 years, and Reu lived 32 plus 207 years; both lived 239 years.

questions.explanation: Reu lived thirty-two years before begetting Serug and another 207 years afterward, totaling 239.

questions.question: Which of these people lived the fewest years?

easy.question: Who was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran?
easy.explanation: The verses say that Terah begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

easy.question: How many of Terah’s sons are mentioned?
easy.explanation: Three sons are mentioned: Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

easy.question: Who was Lot’s father?
easy.explanation: Verse 27 explicitly says that Haran begat Lot.

medium.question: What additional information is given after Terah’s sons are named?
medium.explanation: The verse adds that Haran, Terah’s son, begat Lot.

medium.question: What does “These are the generations of Terah” mean here?
medium.explanation: The phrase introduces Terah’s family line, including his sons and Lot.

medium.question: Which family relationship is correct according to the verses?
answers: Lot begat Haran, and Haran begat Terah
Abram begat Terah, and Terah begat Lot
Terah begat Haran, and Haran begat Lot
medium.explanation: The verses present Terah as Haran’s father and Haran as Lot’s father.

answers: Terah had three sons mentioned here, and Haran had a son named Lot
Terah had only one son, Abram
Lot was the brother of Abram, Nahor, and Haran
challenge.explanation: The verses name Abram, Nahor, and Haran as Terah’s sons and add that Haran begat Lot.

challenge.question: What is the role of verse 27 in relation to verse 26?
answers: It cancels the names of Terah’s sons
It repeats Terah’s sons and adds information about Lot
It describes someone unrelated to Terah
challenge.explanation: Verse 27 repeats the family list and expands it by mentioning Lot.

challenge.question: What was Abram’s relationship to Lot?
challenge.explanation: Abram and Haran were brothers, and Haran was Lot’s father; therefore Abram was Lot’s uncle.

paragraphs.title: Haran Dies in His Native Land

easy.question: Who died according to the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And Haran died.”

easy.question: Where did Haran die?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Haran died in Ur of the Chaldees.

easy.question: Who was Haran’s father?
easy.explanation: The verse identifies Terah as Haran’s father.

medium.question: What relationship is described between Ur of the Chaldees and Haran’s native land?
answers: Ur of the Chaldees was his native land
Ur of the Chaldees was the land of his enemies
Ur of the Chaldees was his destination
medium.explanation: The verse says that Haran died in his native land, namely Ur of the Chaldees.

medium.question: What does “his native land” mean in the phrase “in the land of his nativity”?
answers: The land to which he traveled
The land where he was born
medium.explanation: A native land is the place where a person was born or grew up.

medium.question: What can be understood from “before his father Terah”?
answers: Terah was still alive when Haran died
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that Haran died while his father Terah was still alive.

challenge.question: Which sentence summarizes the verse most accurately?
answers: Haran died in Ur of the Chaldees, his native land, while his father Terah was alive
Haran moved to Ur of the Chaldees and died there many years later
Terah died in Ur of the Chaldees after his son Haran
challenge.explanation: The verse gives all three details: Haran’s death, the location, and his father Terah.

challenge.question: To whom does “his father” refer in “before his father Terah”?
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes Terah in relation to Haran, who had just been mentioned as dying.

challenge.question: Which detail is not stated in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse states the place of Haran’s death and identifies his father, but does not give the cause of death.

easy.question: Who was Nahor’s wife?

medium.question: What does “barren” mean in “Sarai was barren”?

medium.question: Who was the father of Milcah and Iscah?

easy.question: Which land did they intend to reach?

easy.question: Where did they eventually settle?
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying that they came to Haran and dwelt there.

medium.question: What was Lot’s relationship to Terah?
